picks.title: Suno is retiring all of its own AI models, adding tamper-resistant watermarks and capping downloads
picks.excerpt: Suno is retiring all of its current AI models and replacing them with industry-built ones, adding tamper-resistant watermarking and fingerprinting via Audible Magic and Musixmatch Sentinel, and imposing lifetime/monthly download caps that gate commercial release.
picks.rationale: If you release Suno output commercially, the model you built on is being replaced, your files will carry a fingerprint, and how many you can export is now capped.

picks.title: A designer with no DSP background shipped a free analog-style synth in two months with AI-assisted coding
picks.excerpt: OA-Labs released Phosphor-1, a free macOS analog-style synth built for 'controllable instability', with a generative arpeggiator using per-step probability, groove and glitch. The developer — a designer, not a DSP engineer — built it in about two months with AI-assisted coding.
picks.rationale: A free download today and a working proof that a designer can ship a real instrument in two months — per-step probability, groove and glitch included.

picks.title: The new AI chart rules test whether a record is human, never whether the song is
picks.excerpt: New AI chart-eligibility standards police the recording — vocals and masters, the things detection tools can measure — while leaving songwriting untested. The piece argues the industry has quietly redefined 'human' as 'human-performed', not 'human-written'.
picks.rationale: Reads the fine print every artist is about to be judged by: chart eligibility measures your master, not your writing, so AI in the songwriting stage passes.

picks.title: This week's plugin releases lean on machine learning without ever calling themselves AI
picks.excerpt: MusicTech's weekly plugin roundup covers ReStem 2, Lucid, Monochord and Spectral — several leaning on ML for stem separation and synthesis without marketing themselves as AI — alongside Tamber V2.0.
picks.rationale: A week of shipping tools a producer can install now, and evidence that ML has become plumbing rather than a selling point. Build this card on ReStem 2 / Lucid / Monochord / Spectral only — Tamber 2.0 already ran on 08-21.
